title: Appreciation for Terrifier 3, exploitation and bringing audiences along for the ride

commenti.body:
I haven't seen any of the Terrifier movies yet, but I've seen a few clips of the kills on youtube. The one thing I can say I appreciate about the movies is that it kind of brings back the feeling of when I was a kid and watching clips of "Freddy vs. Jason" on youtube, the act of watching felt transgressive, I felt like I was seeing something that I shouldn't be seeing. In the same way, for better or for worse, the fact that Terrifier has built up such a reputation for being nihilistic and mean-spirited has made me overwhelmingly feel for a long time like it's something I didn't want to see, and yet I find it really exciting to watch clips of it on youtube, in a way I haven't felt about a horror movie in a long time. That's not to say I haven't seen any shocking or transgressive films, but I think what sets Terrifier apart is that it's fun in a way that something like Martyrs or Human Centipede isn't. 

I also have to agree that what really sells this movie is Thornton. His performance is magnetic and fun in a way that juxtaposes really well with the awful stuff happening on screen.

If you want to appreciate the series even more, [this literary analysis puts the broader themes into perspective.](https://filmcolossus.com/terrifier-3-explained/)

Leone is getting stronger as he goes, which is cool to see.

I totally agree! A lot of modern horror violence feels sanitized and I think it has to do with 1.) Using CGI instead of prosthetics and practical gore, and 2.) Allowing the camera to linger on the violence. 

I'm not familiar with MPAA rules, but I'm sure the amount of camera time given to violence has an impact on being rated R vs. NC-17, and I think that's why Terrifier just goes for the unrated label. 

The violence in Terrifier feels wrong and it's not fun to watch (especially Terrifier 2), but Thornton is just so charismatic in 3 that I think it helps with the discomfort

I totally agree, to me T3 is far and away the best in the series. I think Leone has come a long way as a filmmaker, T3 was a lot more polished than the prior films, which kind of came off as a little student film-ish to me. I like really hated T2 and I came into T3 as a skeptic, but I am so happy to be proved wrong.

I guess the main thing I'm curious about is what makes the violence so captivating despite it being not fun as you say. Personally I do think that there are absolutely aspects to it that are fun despite being very difficult to watch. I saw the infamous bedroom scene and even though it was rough I felt impressed by the creativity, and the spectacle of it was very entertaining too. 

 Like obviously as you say the actor is charismatic and that helps for sure, but the main attraction at the end of the day is the violence and I wonder what captivated you to it.

I've only watched a little over half of number 2, if you've seen it you can probably guess where I gave up.  Normally, giving up on a movie half way through is a sign it sucks, in this case I can't really say that it did, but it was not for me, sadly.  What I saw of it was incredibly well made, and the effects, especially at the budget they were working at were incredibly. 

And as everyone else has said, Thronton is terrific as Art.  

It really is impressive how much of an impression half a movie can make.

Yeah the bedroom scene is really hard to stomach. It's super impressive from a prosthetics and FX perspective, and honestly it's really bold in how much it wants to show the viewer. But god damn it feels wrong to watch it 😭

I think it's the quality practical FX tbh 

We're so used to CGI gore that never really shows us anything too realistic, so when we have to look at very well-made prosthetics and gore, and the victims are clearly suffering, it just feels too intimate and real. And so you can't look away! I think that's a unique aspect of these movies, hyper realistic violence and gore, but a completely unrealistic premise

Haven’t seen the third yet but the problem with the second movie for me was the filmmakers were so proud of their practical effects that they lingered on them to the point that it just like they were screaming “look at our gore!!!! Look at it!!!”.

It doesn’t actually add anything to the movie.

Not a fan of Leone or the series at all. 

But I have to give him respect for actually pushing the movie out with no MPAA rating. And it seems to be making money with a minimum of controversy. That could be a pretty big deal for future releases

I haven't seen any of them and have just started looking into this one, but I'm so impressed that he refused to play ball with *both* the big studios *and* MPAA that I'm buying a ticket for this weekend knowing next to nothing else about them. 

It feels like we're on the cusp of a very exciting time where independent productions who give audiences what they want are becoming more galvanized, and big studios and the MPAA finally lose their remaining power to creatively undermine and pigeonhole content as a result. The dam could be about to bust wide open at any moment and I'm here for it.
